title: Budget Planning Methodology
overview: Budget methodologies provide frameworks for allocating income across spending categories. The 50/30/20 rule is popular for its simplicity, while zero-based budgeting offers more control.

methods.name: 50/30/20 Rule
methods.description: Popularized by Senator Elizabeth Warren in 'All Your Worth' (2005). Divides after-tax income into three categories: needs, wants, and savings/debt.

formula.name: 50/30/20 Allocation
formula.expression:
Needs: 50% (housing, utilities, groceries, insurance, minimum debt payments)
Wants: 30% (entertainment, dining out, subscriptions, hobbies)
Savings/Debt: 20% (emergency fund, retirement, extra debt payments)

limitations: May not work in high-cost-of-living areas
Needs vs wants can be subjective

methods.name: Zero-Based Budgeting
methods.description: Every dollar is assigned a job. Income minus all allocated expenses equals zero. Provides maximum control and awareness.

formula.name: Zero-Based Principle
formula.expression:
Income - All Expenses - Savings = $0

Every category funded intentionally

methods.name: Pay Yourself First
methods.description: Prioritizes savings by automatically transferring a percentage to savings before other spending. The remainder is used for expenses.

formula.name: Reverse Budgeting
formula.expression:
1. Set savings goal (10-20% of income)
2. Automate transfer to savings
3. Live on remainder

methods.name: Envelope System (Cash-Based)
methods.description: Physical or digital 'envelopes' for each spending category. When envelope is empty, no more spending in that category until next period.

formula.name: Category Limits
formula.expression:
Allocate cash/budget to categories
Spend only from designated envelope
No borrowing between envelopes

limitations: Doesn't work well for irregular expenses

footnotes: Emergency fund goal: 3-6 months of expenses
Recommended savings rate: 15-20% minimum for retirement
Housing should not exceed 28% of gross income (lender guideline)
Total debt payments should not exceed 36% of gross income
disclaimer: Budget frameworks are guidelines. Adjust percentages based on your income, location, and financial goals. What matters most is that you spend less than you earn.
